variables¶

Variable types and censoring classes for conditional transformation models.

class pymlt.variables.CensoredData(exact, lower, upper, trunc_lower=None, trunc_upper=None)[source]¶

Bases: object

Encodes n observations with optional censoring and truncation.

For observation i exactly one censoring pattern is valid:

  • Exact: exact[i] is finite

  • Right-censored: exact[i] is NaN, lower[i] finite, upper[i] = +inf

  • Left-censored: exact[i] is NaN, lower[i] = -inf, upper[i] finite

  • Interval-censored: exact[i] is NaN, both bounds finite

Truncation bounds constrain the observable range: only observations inside [trunc_lower[i], trunc_upper[i]] can appear in the sample.

Parameters:

  • exact (ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]]) – Length-n array. Use np.nan for censored observations.

  • lower (ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]]) – Length-n array of lower bounds. Use -np.inf for left-censored.

  • upper (ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]]) – Length-n array of upper bounds. Use +np.inf for right-censored.

  • trunc_lower (ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]] | None) – Optional length-n array of left truncation points.

  • trunc_upper (ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]] | None) – Optional length-n array of right truncation points.

exact: ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]]¶

class pymlt.variables.NumericVariable(name, support, bounds=None, log_first=False)[source]¶

Bases: object

Continuous numeric variable with a defined support interval.

Parameters:

  • name (str) – Variable name.

  • support (tuple[float, float]) – Closed interval (a, b) defining the domain for the Bernstein basis. Must satisfy a < b.

  • bounds (tuple[float, float] | None) – Optional narrower observation bounds (a, b) with a < b. If None, support is used as bounds.

  • log_first (bool) – If True, apply log-transform before Bernstein evaluation.

bounds: tuple[float, float] | None = None¶
log_first: bool = False¶
